messages.subject: id format problem
parts:
Hi, I am trying to use GGIR to perform a sleep analysis on a CWA-file from 14 days of measurements with the Axivity unit.

I am having trouble getting the id stored in part 2 to match that derived from the sleeplog csv-file and therefore get an error message when running part 4, resulting in no output from part 5.

Here is a breakdown of what I have tried:

1) First I tried using idloc=1 to prompt GGRI to extract the header information on id from the CWA-file. However, in the file part2_summary.csv I could see that no such information was extracted.

2) Then I tried using idloc=2 to prompt GGRI to extract the id from the the first part (before the underscore) of the filename of the CWA-file. This does indeed store a value for id in the file part2_summary.csv, in my case the value 32141, which corresponds to the first column value in my sleeplog, which is also 32141.

Now I expected all to be well. However, GGIR gave the following error message in part 4:

Part 4
 1
Warning: sleeplog id is stored as format: 32141, while
                           code expects format: 32
and later in part 5:

Report part 4
 loading all the milestone data from part 4 this can take a few minutes
Error in g.report.part4(datadir = datadir, metadatadir = metadatadir,  : 
  object 'personSummarynames_backup' not found

Can anybody explain why this is happening? - and possibly a solution?

Best regards, Morten


P.S. I have attached my sleeplog.csv file and the part2_summary.csv file from step 2. Below is the GGIR script I am using:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir=  "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011/Axivity data (CWA)",
             outputdir="E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011",
             f0=1, f1=c(),
             idloc=2, # id number drawn from: 1=file header, 2=numbers before the underscore in the filename
             desiredtz="Europe/Copenhagen",
             overwrite=TRUE, #overwrites previously created milestone data
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,               ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011/sleeplog.csv",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = TRUE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 14,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation

             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

messages.author: 1c8682eea45d1330
messages.subject: Re: id format problem
parts:
Further scrutiny has revealed that the attached .Rdata-file stored in the meta/ms4.out-folder contains a dataframe called "nightsummary" and in this the id-column is stored as 2 digits, in my case "32". But what creates the id-variable in this dataframe and how can I make it use the full 5-digit id "32141" used in previous parts and in my sleeplog?

Hope somebody can help?

Best regards, Morten

messages.author: c98af2c83883e808
messages.subject: Re: id format problem
parts:
Hi Morten,

We have used the sleeplog with the Axivity. 

We used idloc=1. As you say, the id is not extracted in part 2 (column A). However, the filename is in column D of the part2 csv and the id can be extracted from there. In part 4 the id column is extracted and this matched our id in the sleep log.

hope this helps.

Cheers,
Alex

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: id format problem
parts:
HI all,

I recently fixed a bug related to idloc=2 in the development version
of GGIR on GitHub and will include this fix in the next release of
GGIR soon.
Possibly this will address your problem.

More detail about the bug that was fixed:
Using idloc=2 will make that GGIR looks for the ID in the filenmae as
whatever is before the first underscore of the name. However, the code
also automatically excludes the last character of it assuming that
this is a letter as was the case in one of the datasets I worked with.
I realise I never documented this well, hence the confusion also other
users experienced recently.

I have now adapted the code to first check whether the last character
is truly a letter and only exclude the letter if this is the case.

If you want to test this fix immediately then you can work with the
development version of GGIR via the following commands:

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

Do not forget to restart R/Rstudio after installing the package.
Best regards,
Vincent
